sources.title: Evaluating the Instruction-Following Robustness of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, ACL Anthology
sources.publication_status: peer-reviewed conference paper; venue/citation listed by ACL Anthology
sources.content_locator: Abstract, lines 59-60: benchmark evaluates instruction following under prompt injection and reports significant vulnerabilities in tested models.

findings.claim: Adding discussion between agents is conditional rather than an established general win: the ACL 2024 study reports strong prompting can bring a single agent close to the best discussion method, with discussion helping only when demonstrations are absent in its tested reasoning tasks.
findings.decision_implication: A useful research prompt should first elicit and test the decisive assumption, then compare a well-specified single-agent baseline with any proposed extra collaboration step. Preserve the possibility that prompt quality or targeted retrieval is sufficient.
findings.assumptions: Abstract faithfully summarizes the paper; reported benchmark conditions are comparable only to the study's models, prompts and reasoning tasks.
findings.applicability_gap: Not repository investigation, academic literature retrieval, heterogeneous models, or software architecture review; no inference about current Luna/Terra behavior.
findings.next_discriminator: On representative repository decisions, compare a concise evidence-first scout prompt with the current prompt at equal retrieval budget; independently score sourced alternative discovery and expert decision usefulness.

findings.claim: A useful literature-scout report needs separate checks for citation accuracy, factual correctness, topic coverage and coherence; citation-backed prose alone is not adequate evaluation.
findings.support_locator: Nature article, ScholarQABench evaluation discussion, lines 107 onward
findings.decision_implication: Prompt for primary sources, publication status, exact support locators, coverage and applicability limits, and evaluate those dimensions separately. Keep the expert able to open decisive papers directly.
findings.assumptions: The paper's scientific-query synthesis task gives relevant evaluation dimensions, not a ready-validated prompt for software-engineering scouts.
findings.applicability_gap: OpenScholar uses a scientific corpus/retriever and a literature-synthesis benchmark; it does not establish that ordinary web search or a small-model scout will achieve comparable citation quality or recall.
findings.next_discriminator: Blindly audit a small sample of reports against source passages and expert-selected relevant papers, scoring claim support, missed contrary evidence, and decision utility separately.

findings.claim: Subagent handoff can be a major silent failure point in repository-level Q&A: one 2026 preprint abstract reports 41.8% of deep-agentic-search failures at planner/sub-agent handoff and lower accuracy/cost results than semantic search in its SWE-QA setup.
findings.support_locator: arXiv abstract; study reports 65.2% semantic-search accuracy vs 46.2% deep-agentic-search and 41.8% handoff-associated share of deep-search failures
findings.decision_implication: Require a compact evidence trail that lets the coordinator/expert verify the scout's conclusion at source, and treat missing or mismatched support as an explicit handoff failure. Consider simpler targeted retrieval for straightforward read-only facts.
findings.assumptions: Abstract's operational definitions and reported benchmark results are accurate; this is preliminary evidence because reviewed publication status was not established.
findings.applicability_gap: One preprint, read-only repository QA and indexed repositories; not open-ended architecture research, our repository or mixed-model tasks. It does not establish that delegating investigations is generally inferior.
findings.next_discriminator: For matched factual repository questions, compare scout handoffs with direct expert retrieval and record source-location agreement and silent error rate.

findings.claim: Retrieved text creates an instruction-following risk that must be measured independently from evidence quality; the EMNLP benchmark abstract reports significant injection vulnerabilities in the tested instruction-following models.
findings.decision_implication: Keep browsed pages as untrusted evidence, state source provenance, and prohibit external text from changing the task, permissions or tools; do not interpret compliance with this prompt as a security guarantee.
findings.assumptions: Abstract-level result generalizes only cautiously beyond the tested models and attack benchmark.
findings.applicability_gap: The paper evaluates robustness, not the effectiveness of any specific boundary wording in this workflow or these models.
findings.next_discriminator: If validating the workflow, separately audit whether source-origin instructions altered scope or tool use; do not infer safety from successful research outputs.

rejected_or_redundant: Did not use ICML 2024 debate-strategy result in a finding: opened PMLR page confirmed publication metadata but the relevant content was not retained in the opened excerpt; abstract-level corroboration was insufficient for the content constraint.

Agentless and broader multi-agent software-engineering papers were not developed into claims because the stronger direct repository-search result already supplied a close empirical handoff comparison and task asks for investigation workflow rather than patching performance.
unresolved: No retrieved peer-reviewed empirical study directly tests prompts for smaller-model subagents researching academic alternatives for mixed-model software architecture decisions.
Actual Luna performance, cost, accuracy, model identity, prompt effects, and expert-review burden were not measured; this case provides literature-informed hypotheses only.

The retrieved-research limitations are constrained by the 16-operation total, and the search ceiling was exceeded: 10 search queries were issued although the contract allowed at most 8. Six opens were used; total logical operations reached 16. No more web operations were performed after noticing this accounting error.
stop_reason: Reached the 16-operation total budget; further source verification stopped. Wall time stayed under the 12-minute target.
escalation_ready: For Sol/Astra review: favor a prompt that asks a scout to identify the decision-critical assumption, search primary work for confirmation and counterevidence, map study conditions to the repository/model at hand, and return a short traceable evidence set with explicit gaps. Compare it against a strong single-agent prompt before adding debate or more agents; keep direct expert access to sources and independent patch acceptance. This is a testable workflow candidate, not an evidence-backed claim of improvement. The operation accounting exceeded the query-count ceiling, so treat coverage as bounded and do not treat this run as compliant with that specific limit.
